task: Implement the SmartTube AI subtitle plan (T01/T02): bind the actually selected subtitle track to its exact source, prove the original-cue baseline, and design the single write entry to SubtitleView. Decide for each claim whether the quoted evidence supports it, contradicts it, or is insufficient.

checks.claim: The subtitle Format instance created while parsing the manifest reaches the selected MediaTrack as the same object, so an identity map keyed by Format, built from the manifest the player really uses, binds the actually selected track.
Turning subtitles off is observable without inventing a new flag: the subtitle renderer's selected track becomes an empty SubtitleTrack with format == null and groupIndex == -1.

The existing onTracksChanged loop cannot report that subtitles were turned off, because a disabled renderer contributes a null element that the loop skips, so an explicit subtitle state must be emitted.

Comparing a subtitle representation baseUrl with MediaSubtitle.getBaseUrl() identifies the exact source even when tracks share vssId, because a derived translation track appends &tlang= to the original URL.

Matching subtitle candidates only by Format.id (vssId) or by display name cannot uniquely identify a source, so a binder must verify uniqueness and refuse an ambiguous result instead of taking the first candidate.
OriginalSubtitleNormalizer reproduces the removed inline behavior for every cue shape the decoder produces; passing null-text cues through instead of throwing is the only intended deviation.

Nothing resets the incremental subtitle buffer on seek or track change, so a line buffered for the previous subtitle source can strip text from the next source until the buffer happens to be replaced.

The upstream PR patch adds a second, listener-bypassing writer to the SubtitleView in addition to onCues, so copying it verbatim would create two independent writers that bypass source-identity checks.
